findings.title: New contextual logger middleware and the moved log fields have no test
findings.body: NewContextualLoggerMiddleware (lines 14-20) and instrumentContext (lines 27-37) are new, and LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now gets pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID only from the context attributes this middleware writes (logger_middleware.go:58). No test in this directory checks either side. Other middlewares here have test files (tracing_middleware_test.go, user_header_middleware_test.go). A test that wraps the contextual middleware and the logger middleware, and asserts those fields on the 'Plugin Request Completed' line, would catch a future reorder or a missing attribute.

findings.title: Test name still refers to the removed InstrumentationMiddleware
findings.body: The test is named TestInstrumentationMiddleware, but it now builds and tests MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware at line 78). Renaming it to TestMetricsMiddleware would match the type it covers.

findings.title: Ordering between the contextual logger and LoggerMiddleware is now load-bearing but undocumented
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware (logger_middleware.go:58) no longer sets pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName or dsUID itself. It relies on ContextualLoggerMiddleware, placed above it here, having put them on ctx. If someone moves the contextual middleware below the logger middleware, or builds the logger middleware without it, the egress log line loses those fields silently. The sentence that told readers to keep the instrumentation middleware at the top of the stack was removed with this change, and nothing replaces it. A short comment at this list, or on NewContextualLoggerMiddleware, saying it must precede LoggerMiddleware would close the gap.

findings.title: Doc says the middleware adds a contextual logger, but it adds log attributes
findings.body: The doc comment on NewContextualLoggerMiddleware (lines 12-13), and the one on instrumentContext (line 26), say the middleware adds a contextual logger to the context. The code only calls log.WithContextualAttributes (line 36). The logger is derived later, when a caller runs FromContext (pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217). Wording such as 'adds contextual log attributes' would match the code.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext drops calls made through the fake it was called on
findings.body: FromContext returns a new TestLogger and ignores the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now writes its completion line with m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info (logger_middleware.go:58). Before this change that call recorded on the fake the test passed in. Now it records on a fresh, unreachable fake, so a test that passes a TestLogger to NewLoggerMiddleware and checks InfoLogs would see zero calls and no failure. No current test does this; NewLoggerMiddleware is only constructed in pluginsintegration.go:161. Returning the receiver (f) would keep the recorded calls visible to the test that holds the fake.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware writes 'Plugin Request Completed' using m.logger.FromContext(ctx) and context-derived fields
contracts.before_after: Before (removed lines in the diff): logger_middleware.go built pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName and dsUID itself and called m.logger.Info. After: those fields come from the attributes ContextualLoggerMiddleware writes to ctx; the logger reads them through the registered provider (pkg/infra/log/log.go:55-61) and ConcreteLogger.FromContext (pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217). The middleware order is set in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go:157-161 and applied by pkg/plugins/manager/client/decorator.go:101-109, so the contextual middleware runs before the logger middleware.
contracts.visible_effect: Each 'Plugin Request Completed' line keeps the same keys and values. Field order in the logfmt line may differ, because contextual keys are bound before the call's keys.
contracts.failure_mode: If ctx lacks the attributes, the line is written without pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID, with no error. This happens if ContextualLoggerMiddleware is moved below LoggerMiddleware, or if LoggerMiddleware runs without it.

contracts.action: ContextualLoggerMiddleware adds plugin and request attributes to ctx for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics
contracts.before_after: Before (removed lines in the diff): instrumentPluginRequest called instrumentContext after the pluginTarget check and before next. After: a separate middleware placed after Tracing and Metrics adds the same attributes for the same four endpoints. SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream pass through in both versions. The pluginTarget error still returns before any attributes are added, because the Metrics middleware runs first.
contracts.visible_effect: The same attributes appear on the same calls. Metrics labels and values are unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: None in this middleware: it is pure and has no error path. If the plugin is not registered, Metrics returns plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered before the contextual middleware runs, which matches the old behaviour.

contracts.action: traceID on plugin request log lines (moved from explicit logParams to the context provider)
contracts.before_after: Before (removed lines in the diff): logger_middleware.go called tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended traceID. After: a contextual log provider registered in tracing.ProvideService makes the same call with the same requireSampled=false flag.
contracts.visible_effect: traceID still appears on the line when the request carries a trace ID, provided the provider is registered.
contracts.failure_mode: If the provider is never registered (ProvideService never runs on some production path), traceID is silently absent from these lines, with no error.
contracts.open_question: Does every production path that builds the tracer used by CreateMiddlewares call tracing.ProvideService, so the traceID provider is always registered?

contracts.before_after: The wrapper asserts the result of ConcreteLogger.FromContext to *ConcreteLogger. On failure it returns d.New(), which drops the context attributes.
contracts.failure_mode: The fallback cannot be reached: ConcreteLogger.FromContext returns either cl.New(...) (log.go:219, a *ConcreteLogger) or cl itself. If it were reached, attributes would be dropped with no error.

contracts.before_after: Before: LoggerMiddleware called m.logger.Info on the fake the test passed in, so its InfoLogs recorded the call. After: the call goes to a fresh TestLogger from FromContext, so the passed-in fake's InfoLogs stay empty. The New method at fake.go:18-20 already uses the same fresh-logger pattern.
contracts.failure_mode: A test that passes a TestLogger into NewLoggerMiddleware and checks InfoLogs sees zero calls. No current test does this; NewLoggerMiddleware is constructed only in pluginsintegration.go:161.

summary: No blocker or fix. The change moves LoggerMiddleware's log fields onto context attributes that ContextualLoggerMiddleware sets, and the wiring order (Tracing, Metrics, ContextualLogger, Logger) makes that work. The traceID field now comes from the tracing context provider with the same requireSampled=false flag. The Logger interface gained FromContext; the only implementers in pkg/plugins/log are the wrapper and TestLogger, and both implement it. Findings are consider-level: missing tests for the new middleware and the moved fields, a stale test name, an undocumented ordering dependency, a docstring that calls attributes a logger, and a test fake whose FromContext drops recorded calls. One contract (traceID registration on every production path) is open.
